newsitem.title: USA: FAA says evaluating aircraft ice-warning system.
newsitem.headline: FAA says evaluating aircraft ice-warning system.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said on Monday it was evaluating new ultrasonic technology to warn pilots of potentially dangerous ice build-up on aircraft wings.
The system was designed by Rosemount Aerospace Inc, a member of the B.F. Goodrich Co aerospace companies, in conjunction with McDonnell Douglas Corp, Northwest Airlines Corp and FBS Inc.
The HALO Ground Ice Detection System uses two ultrasonic sensors on each wing to detect ice and other frozen contaminants on aircraft wings and displays the information in the cockpit.
An in-service evaluation carried out last winter by Rosemount and Northwest, using two McDonnell Douglas MD-82 airliners, showed that the system could successfully detect ice build-up, the FAA said.
Rosemount is now working with the FAA to gain approval for the system, the FAA said.
